content:
Fatigue can feel like overwhelming exhaustion rather than ordinary tiredness. In inflammatory arthritis it may affect concentration and daily activities, and rest does not always relieve it.

This guide is general information, not a diagnosis or personal treatment plan. New or worsening fatigue should not automatically be put down to arthritis.

Why fatigue needs an individual assessment

Inflammation, pain, poor sleep, mood, medicines and other health conditions can all matter. Anaemia, thyroid problems and sleep apnoea are among the possible causes of persistent tiredness. Your GP or rheumatology team can review the pattern, your medicines and whether tests are needed.

NICE NG100, recommendation 1.7.1, includes fatigue among the effects of rheumatoid arthritis that should be assessed by the multidisciplinary team. This is rheumatoid arthritis guidance, not proof that every cause of fatigue has the same treatment.

Options to discuss with your team

  • Plan activity and rest: notice which tasks use most energy, break demanding jobs into smaller parts and discuss a workable balance with your team.
  • Choose activity that fits your health: tailored physical activity can help fatigue in inflammatory rheumatic conditions. Ask a physiotherapist about your symptoms, ability and other conditions rather than following a fixed increase in exercise.
  • Review sleep: a regular sleep routine may help. Tell your GP about loud snoring, gasping during sleep or persistent daytime sleepiness.
  • Review disease control and other causes: new or worsening fatigue may prompt a review of inflammatory disease activity, pain, mood, medicines and other health problems. Do not change prescribed treatment yourself.
  • Ask about structured support: EULAR recommends access to tailored psychoeducational support for fatigue in inflammatory rheumatic conditions. This goes beyond simply being told to rest or think positively.

The 2023 EULAR fatigue recommendations support tailored physical activity and psychoeducational interventions in inflammatory rheumatic conditions. They do not establish one exercise programme for every person with arthritis or unexplained exhaustion.

If activity causes a delayed worsening of symptoms, tell your clinician. For people with ME/CFS, NICE NG206 advises against exercise programmes with fixed increases in activity. Do not use general arthritis exercise advice to override an individual ME/CFS plan.

When to arrange a review

Contact your GP or rheumatology team if fatigue is new, worsening or affecting daily life. The NHS advises a GP review for unexplained tiredness lasting a few weeks, tiredness affecting daily life, or tiredness with other symptoms such as weight loss or mood changes.

A short diary of sleep, activity, symptoms and medicines may help you describe what is happening. It is not a diagnostic test. Never stop or change prescribed medicine yourself; ask your GP or pharmacist for a review.

When to get urgent help

Call 999 or go to A&E if someone suddenly becomes confused. Do not assume this is ordinary fatigue or a medicine effect. Do not drive to A&E. Ask someone else to drive or call 999. Stay with the person and reassure them while help is arranged. See NHS sudden confusion advice.

Call 999 for severe difficulty breathing, chest pain that is sudden and does not go away or comes with sweating, sickness, light-headedness or breathlessness, or signs of a stroke such as a drooping face, arm weakness or speech difficulty. After a fall, call 999 if the person cannot get up or may have injured their head, back, neck or hip. See NHS advice on breathlessness, chest pain, stroke and falls.

Get urgent medical advice for sudden severe joint pain, difficulty moving or putting weight on a joint, or a hot, swollen joint, even if you do not have a fever. Do not wait to see whether rest improves it. In England, Scotland and Wales, contact an urgent GP service or call 111. In Northern Ireland, contact your GP or GP out-of-hours service. See NHS septic arthritis advice.

Common questions

Can exercise help fatigue?

Tailored physical activity can help fatigue in inflammatory rheumatic conditions, but the plan should fit your health, disease activity and preferences. Unexplained fatigue, other illnesses and a delayed worsening after activity need assessment rather than a universal exercise prescription.

Does fatigue mean my arthritis is active?

It can be related to inflammatory disease activity, but it can also persist when inflammation is controlled or have another cause. Tell your team rather than changing medicines yourself.
